decisions.statement: A module reading an add-on's own global as it loads reaches the module setting that global.
An add-on's own globals are the values its declaration files declare.
A declaration file is an add-on's where the add-on's page names it among its parts.
A name the game's declarations state is the game's, and is never judged.
A module is an add-on's where it sits under the tree of the add-on's page.
A name is read at load where a top-level statement spells it as a bare identifier.
A name spelled in a function body, a class body or a type is read later, if at all.
A name the module binds is that binding rather than the add-on's global.
Which names a statement reads at load is answered by `load-order` rather than here.
A module sets a name where a statement running at load assigns through the global table.
The global table is `globalThis`, `_G`, a call handed one of those alone, or a top-level alias.
A key spelled as a string literal sets the name it spells.
A key bound by a loop over a top-level table of string literals sets every literal in it.
A bare assignment to a name the module binds nowhere sets the global of that name.
A key bound any other way is untraceable, and its assignment sets nothing.
An untraceable setter is no setter, so a fault behind it is missed rather than invented.
A name no module of its add-on sets is not judged.
A reader reaching any one setter of a name is in order.
A module reaches itself.
What a module reaches is answered by the at-load predicate rather than walked here.
The closure is taken once per add-on, from its bundle entry and every module under its tree.
A module spelling none of the add-on's names is not parsed.
At change only a module the change has is refused, and its add-on is read whole around it.
At audit every module of every add-on is judged.
A refusal names the reader, the names read, and the setters the reader does not reach.
Names one reader misses through one set of setters are refused together.
A bare assignment inside a function body sets its global when called rather than as the body loads.
A module outside every add-on's tree sets no global this check traces.
A read through the global table itself is not judged.
The order of statements inside one module is not judged here.

definition: the check refusing a module that reads an add-on's own global before the module setting it has run
